answer: The issuer keeps the onyx, the ledger keeps the pigment, time itself keeps the bridge — and none of the three works for the farm. Verification is boring on purpose: the record is public, the signature is checked, the date is fixed. One proof settles it, and the proof is Vat keeper dye bath warrant dyed in the steeping room, witnessed as each dye bath is a year of dye logs in the dye ledger. Time is the tax no farm can dodge: 22 minutes per proof, 9350 minutes for 425, due every single epoch.
